nodes.name: Shaam ke 7 baje
nodes.notes: 19:00 IST, the hour the shutter comes half down and the merchant finally looks at their phone. The workflow's timezone is Asia/Kolkata, so the cron reads in local shop time.

nodes.name: On demand
nodes.notes: The demo lever: POST an empty body with X-Munshiji-Token to run the digest on cue instead of waiting for 19:00.

nodes.name: Fetch merchant
nodes.notes: First fetch decides the digest's language: merchant.language is 'hi' for the seeded shop.

nodes.name: Fetch dashboard
nodes.notes: Chained after Fetch merchant, never beside it: two branches into one node make that node run once per branch.

nodes.name: Fetch insights
nodes.notes: GET the stored feed, deliberately not POST /api/insights/default/refresh: refresh reruns every engine and takes as long as it takes. An on-stage canvas must contain zero unbounded-latency nodes; the backend refreshes on its own schedule.

nodes.name: Fetch pending actions
nodes.notes: status=pending_approval is the ActionStatus enum value the API filters on - the digest only ever pitches something still waiting for a yes.

nodes.name: WhatsApp: send and wait
nodes.notes: Credential is deliberately unselected: open the node and pick your own WhatsApp Business Cloud (Meta) credential, then choose the sender in 'Phone Number ID'. Recipient is $vars.MERCHANT_WHATSAPP - the merchant's own verified phone, which is why this node ships enabled while the customer-facing sender in munshiji-actions ships disabled. If Meta setup stalls tonight, swap this single node for Telegram sendAndWait - same mechanics. The wait resumes by itself after 12 hours so a digest ignored overnight cannot pile up.

nodes.name: Approved with something to send?
nodes.notes: The sendAndWait approval resumes with { data: { approved: true|false } }. Both must hold: the merchant tapped हाँ भेज दो AND the digest actually carried a pending action - an approval of a digest with nothing to send approves nothing.

nodes.name: Approve the action
nodes.notes: Hits the same approval gate the app's own screen uses: the backend records consent, then executes through the action provider. approved_by is ApproveIn's only field.
